result: Two dated agent-lab runs of protocol document-retrieval-preregistration-v2 exist and are peer-executed, not mine. Run 1 (out/20260922T055714Z, started 05:57:14Z) is an INCOMPLETE prior attempt: arm-1 (hybrid) did not run its preregistered backend configuration and every arm-1 metric is null (decision D6: 'the arm did not run its preregistered backend configuration'). Run 2 (out/20260922T060810Z, started 06:10:14Z) is the COMPLETE, later run: arm-1's dense lane was supplied an embedding pass and both arms scored on the sealed snapshot with repeat=3. Measured: BM25 (arm-0) recall_at_3=0.6667, recall_at_1=0.4167, mrr=0.5688; hybrid (arm-1) recall_at_3=0.8333, recall_at_1=0.5833, mrr=0.7319 -- hybrid beats BM25 on all three closure-gating metrics by more than the preregistered delta thresholds (closure.json's reasons array shows each comparison evaluating to true). The ONLY remaining closure blocker in run 2 is a missing metric: latency_p95_ms is null for both arms, with null_reasons citing decision D12, 'cli_cannot_target_disposable_snapshot' -- the runner's CLI wrapper cannot point its own latency-timing path at a disposable/sealed snapshot copy, so no comparable p95 latency number can be produced under the sealed protocol as currently implemented. Because of this single missing metric, tools/compare/closure.mjs reports status "unresolved" for both runs (not "retain" or "overturn"), and the protocol's own status_scope note states explicitly that even a full closure here would establish only the retrieval-fidelity/abstention/returned-context sub-claim, not the full incumbent overturn_when (which also needs answer-fidelity, measured-task-cost and native-client-behaviour evidence). The sealed protocol also declares a third arm (arm-2, a difficult-layout parser lane) that was NEVER executed (install_required true, no install-receipt.json present), so the two runs cover only markdown BM25 vs hybrid, not difficult-layout documents.

verdict_impact.explanation: This citation does not itself change any catalog verdict (it is read-only), but it corrects the triage's characterization of document-retrieval gap 1 ('no full corpus seal ... establishes no general ranking or token saving') and reinforces the critic's correction: a sealed-snapshot comparison DOES exist and DOES show hybrid materially ahead of BM25 on recall_at_3/recall_at_1/mrr with repeat=3, which weakens the current BM25-favoring decision text in catalogs/landscape/foundation.json (not edited here, per the binding rule against editing catalogs). The remaining blocker is narrower than 'no comparison exists': it is specifically the missing latency_p95_ms metric (decision D12) and the never-executed difficult-layout arm-2. A future check that resolves D12 (lets the runner target a disposable snapshot for timing) or executes arm-2 would be the next decision-changing step, not another repeat of this same read.
